mainTopic: Blemishes found after betrothal: who must bring proof, and how presumptions are weighed
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a husband who finds blemishes on his wife and claims the betrothal was a מקח טעות. He cannot claim this for visible blemishes, or for hidden ones if the town has a bathhouse. The גמרא notices that the רישא sounds like רבי יהושע while the סיפא sounds like רבן גמליאל, and רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is split between two תנאים. רבא then shows that רבי יהושע sets aside חזקה דגופא only when a חזקה דממונא opposes it, and proves this from a ברייתא about צרעת. רבא also gives his own answer: blemishes are assumed to have started where they were found, so both halves of the משנה follow one rule. אביי challenges this from the משנה's words 'before she was betrothed.' After one defense is rejected, the גמרא explains that after betrothal two presumptions work against the husband. The weighing against his own presumption finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Visible blemishes, and hidden ones in a town with a bathhouse, cannot be claimed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends: a husband cannot complain about visible blemishes. If the town has a bathhouse, he cannot complain about hidden blemishes either, because he could have had his female relatives check her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for blemishes that can be seen, he cannot make a claim. And if there is a bathhouse in that city, he cannot claim even about hidden blemishes, because he checks her through his female relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rules about a husband who finds blemishes on his wife and wants to cancel the betrothal. It lists cases where his complaint is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With visible blemishes, we assume he saw them before the betrothal and accepted them. With hidden blemishes, if there is a public bathhouse, we assume he sent his female relatives to look, so he cannot say he did not know. Either way, the betrothal is not treated as a מקח טעות.

keyTerms.meaning: Visible blemishes
Hidden blemishes, on parts of the body that are normally covered
To make a claim (here, that the betrothal was a mistake)
Bathhouse
His female relatives

phrases.english: But with regard to visible blemishes
he cannot make a claim.
phrases.notes: His claim would be that the betrothal was a mistake. Since he could see these blemishes, we assume he accepted them.

phrases.english: And if there is a bathhouse in that city,
even about hidden blemishes
he cannot make a claim,
because he checks her through his female relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּמוּמִין שֶׁבַּגָּלוּי אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִטְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband cannot claim a מקח טעות for visible blemishes. In a town with a bathhouse, he also cannot claim it for hidden blemishes.

steps.title: Inference from the first clause: without proof, the husband is believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the רישא of the משנה closely. Since the father must bring proof, without proof the husband is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the father wins is that he brings proof. But if the father does not bring proof, the husband is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a precise inference from the first part of the משנה. This sets up the question of which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא says that while she is still in her father's house, the father must prove the blemishes appeared after the betrothal. The גמרא draws the flip side: if the father cannot prove it, the husband's claim stands. So the woman's side does not win just by her body's presumed earlier state.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is..., used to open a precise inference
But (the flip side), used to draw the opposite case
Proof
Is believed

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that the father brings proof,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier part of the משנה: if the blemishes are found while she's in her father's house, the father must prove they came after the betrothal.

phrases.english: but if the father does not bring proof,
the husband is believed.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letter ה in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמַיְיתֵי הָאָב רְאָיָה, הָא לָא מַיְיתֵי הָאָב רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by drawing an inference from the רישא of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the רישא: if the father has no proof, the husband is believed.

steps.title: Whose view is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the husband is believed without proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the inference in Step 2 matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מסכתא there is a מחלוקת about whether a woman's claim about her body is accepted against her husband. The גמרא wants to know which side of that מחלוקת our משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is it?

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the view inferred in Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that without proof the husband is believed against the father's side.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהושע: we don't rely on her word
steps.stepSummary: The רישא follows רבי יהושע, who said in an earlier משנה that we do not rely on the woman's own word.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהושע, who said: we do not live by her mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רישא matches רבי יהושע, who does not accept the woman's side without proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, a woman claims something happened to her after the betrothal and the husband says it happened before. רבי יהושע says her word alone is not enough. Our רישא makes the same kind of demand: the father's side needs proof, or the husband wins.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who does not accept the woman's claim without proof
We do not live by her mouth, meaning we don't rely on her word alone

phrases.english: It is רבי יהושע, who said:
We do not live from her mouth.
phrases.notes: This quotes a משנה earlier in the מסכתא (דף יב): her word alone isn't enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, דְּאָמַר: לָא מִפִּיהָ אָנוּ חַיִּין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רישא follows רבי יהושע, who requires the woman's side to prove its claim.

steps.title: But the second clause sounds like רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says the husband must bring proof once she is in his domain. Without his proof, the father is believed, which matches רבן גמליאל, not רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part: if she entered the husband's domain, the husband must bring proof. The reason is that he brings proof. But if he does not bring proof, the father is believed. So we have arrived at רבן גמליאל, who said she is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of inference from the סיפא and finds it matches the opposite opinion. So the רישא and סיפא seem to follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the burden of proof is on the husband, so without proof the father's side wins. That fits רבן גמליאל, who believes the woman. The problem is that one משנה should not follow רבי יהושע in its first half and רבן גמליאל in its second half.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause; used to bring up the end of the משנה
The husband's domain, after she has moved in with him
We have arrived at (another opinion)
The תנא who believes the woman's claim
She is believed

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: in the רישא the father carries the burden of proof, but in the סיפא the husband does. That switch is exactly what makes the two halves sound like two different תנאים.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
If she entered the husband's domain,
the husband must bring proof.
The reason is that the husband brings proof,
but if the husband does not bring proof,
the father is believed.
We have arrived at רבן גמליאל,
who said she is believed!
phrases.notes: This is the same earlier case. רבן גמליאל disagrees with רבי יהושע and accepts her word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of inference to the סיפא and finds it contradicts the answer of Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא implies the father is believed without proof, which is רבן גמליאל's view. So the רישא and סיפא follow opposite תנאים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the משנה is split between two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר accepts that the two halves follow different opinions. The תנא who taught one half did not teach the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is broken. The one who taught this did not teach that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction by saying the משנה really is split. The רישא and סיפא come from different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reinterpreting either half, רבי אלעזר admits the problem: the רישא follows רבי יהושע and the סיפא follows רבן גמליאל. The משנה is treated as combining two views rather than one consistent opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is broken, meaning the משנה is split and not one unit

keyTerms.term: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Whoever taught this half did not teach that half

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, our משנה is split: the רישא follows רבי יהושע (the woman's side needs proof) and the סיפא follows רבן גמליאל (the husband needs proof).

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
It is broken;
phrases.notes: He means the משנה doesn't hold together as one opinion.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁשָּׁנָה זוֹ לֹא שָׁנָה זוֹ.
phrases.english: whoever taught this did not teach that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source between two authors
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה was assumed to follow one תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא and סיפא follow two different תנאים.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יהושע ignores the body's presumption only against a money presumption
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רבי יהושע's view. He does not reject חזקה דגופא entirely. He sets it aside only when a חזקה דממונא opposes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do not say that רבי יהושע never follows the presumption of the body. Rather, רבי יהושע does not follow the presumption of the body only where there is a monetary presumption against it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא clarifies exactly how far רבי יהושע's opinion, cited in step 4, goes. He says it is not a total rejection of חזקה דגופא, and the next steps finish and prove this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think רבי יהושע never trusts the presumption that a body stays in its earlier state. רבא says he does trust it in general. He overrides it only when it would take money from someone who already holds it, as in רבי יהושע's case, where she wants payment from the husband. So רבי יהושע's ruling there is a special outcome caused by the money presumption, not a rejection of חזקה דגופא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say; introduces a correction of a possible mistaken idea
After; with אָזֵיל it means to follow or rely on
Presumption of the body: a body is assumed to stay as it was until shown otherwise
Monetary presumption: money stays with whoever holds it until proven otherwise

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the scope of רבי יהושע's opinion. A presumption about the body loses only when it is up against a presumption of who holds the money, and that idea shapes how the משנה can be read.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Do not say that רבי יהושע

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָזֵיל בָּתַר חֲזָקָה דְגוּפָא כְּלָל,
phrases.english: does not follow the presumption of the body at all;
phrases.notes: This means we assume a person's body stayed the way it was, until proven otherwise.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כִּי לָא אָזֵיל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: rather, when רבי יהושע does not follow
the presumption of the body,
it is where there is a monetary presumption.
phrases.notes: The monetary presumption means money stays with whoever is holding it, here the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לָא אָזֵיל בָּתַר חֲזָקָה דְגוּפָא כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's רישא was tied to רבי יהושע (step 4), רבא clarifies how far רבי יהושע's view goes. This is a side clarification. רבא's own alternative answer to the contradiction comes separately in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע sets aside חזקה דגופא only when a חזקה דממונא stands against it.

steps.title: Where no money is at stake, רבי יהושע follows the body's presumption
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the previous statement: when there is no חזקה דממונא, רבי יהושע does rely on חזקה דגופא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where there is no presumption about who holds the money, רבי יהושע does follow the presumption about the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the limit from the last step. רבי יהושע only sets aside חזקה דגופא when money is involved; otherwise he follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said רבי יהושע ignores חזקה דגופא when a חזקה דממונא stands against it. This line gives the other side: alone, חזקה דגופא is something he accepts. The next step will bring a proof for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumption based on who currently holds the money
Presumption about a person's body, that it stays in its earlier state
Where there is not
Goes after, follows

phrases.english: But where there is no presumption of money,

phrases.aramaic: אָזֵיל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בָּתַר חֲזָקָה דְגוּפָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua does follow the presumption of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the limiting statement in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without an opposing חזקה דממונא, רבי יהושע relies on חזקה דגופא.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא about a white spot and white hair
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on צרעת: if it is unclear whether the spot or the white hair came first, the תנא קמא says impure, and רבי יהושע says 'כהה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: if the bright spot came before the white hair, the person is impure. If the white hair came before the spot, he is pure. If it is unclear, he is impure. רבי יהושע says: 'dull'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהושע follows חזקה דגופא when no money is involved. The meaning of his one word 'כהה' will be explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White hair only makes a בהרת impure if the hair grew after the spot. When we are unsure of the order, the first opinion says impure. רבי יהושע disagrees, and since this case has nothing to do with money, it is a clean test of how he treats the body's earlier, pure state.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white spot on the skin, a type of צרעת
White hair growing in the spot, a sign of impurity
Ritually impure
Ritually pure
A case of doubt

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קוֹדֵם לְשֵׂעָר לָבָן — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: If the bright spot came before the white hair, he is impure;

phrases.aramaic: אִם שֵׂעָר לָבָן קוֹדֵם לַבַּהֶרֶת — טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: if the white hair came before the bright spot, he is pure;
if it is uncertain, he is impure.
And Rabbi Yehoshua says: Dull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the claim in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע follows חזקה דגופא when no money is involved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about the order of a בהרת and white hair.

steps.title: What does 'dull' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע meant by the word 'כהה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יהושע's short word means. This sets up the answer that will finish the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if 'כהה' shows that רבי יהושע rules pure in the case of doubt. So the word must be explained before the proof is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: What is
Dull, faded in color

phrases.english: What is 'dull'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי יהושע's word in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי יהושע's ruling 'כהה'.

steps.title: רבה explains: 'dull' means pure
steps.stepSummary: רבה says 'כהה' means the person is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains that רבי יהושע rules the person pure in the case of doubt. This finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dull spot is not an impure נגע, so 'כהה' is a way of saying 'pure'. In a doubt with no money involved, רבי יהושע keeps the body in its earlier pure state. That is exactly following חזקה דגופא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains רבי יהושע's word
Dull means pure, like a faded spot that is not impure

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע ignores חזקה דגופא only when money is involved. In a pure ritual case like צרעת, he follows it and rules pure.

phrases.english: Rabba said: 'Dull' means pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 and completes the proof of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כהה' means pure, so רבי יהושע follows חזקה דגופא here.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: blemishes started where they were found
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains both halves of the משנה with one rule: blemishes are assumed to have started in the place where they were found.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: In the first part, they were found here, so they were here. In the second part too, they were found here, so they were here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the contradiction from step 5. He says the whole משנה follows one rule, so there is no need to split it between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the blemishes were found in the father's house, so we assume they were there before the betrothal, and the father must prove otherwise. In the סיפא, they were found in the husband's house, so we assume they started there, and the husband must bring proof. One simple rule explains both halves.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The later part of the משנה
They were found here, so they were here

steps.confusionAlert: Each half has its own 'here'. In the רישא it means the father's house, and in the סיפא it means the husband's house.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a different answer from רבי אלעזר's approach in step 6. It keeps the משנה as one consistent teaching instead of two different opinions.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The first clause: they were found here, and they were here.
phrases.notes: Here means the father's house. Since the blemishes showed up there, we assume they were already there before the betrothal.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא נָמֵי, כָּאן נִמְצְאוּ וְכָאן הָיוּ.
phrases.english: The latter clause too: they were found here, and they were here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different solution to step 5 than רבי אלעזר's split in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying principle: one presumption explains both clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא and סיפא contradict each other and must follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses follow one rule: blemishes are assumed to have begun where they were found.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the words 'before she was betrothed'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה requires the husband to prove the blemishes existed before betrothal. Proof that they existed after betrothal, while she was still in her father's house, is not enough. By רבא's rule, it should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: The משנה says if she entered the husband's domain, the husband must prove she had these blemishes before she was betrothed, so his deal was a mistaken deal. Before betrothal, yes. From after betrothal, no. But why? Let us say: they were found here, so they were here!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's rule using the exact wording of the משנה. If רבא were right, showing the blemishes existed after betrothal should be enough proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'before she was betrothed', which implies that proof of blemishes only after betrothal does not help. But with רבא's rule, if the husband proves they were present in the father's house after betrothal, we should assume they were there before betrothal too. So the משנה seems to reject רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from a source
The husband's domain, after the wedding
She becomes betrothed
A mistaken deal, which can be undone
Blemishes

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
If she entered the husband's domain,
the husband must bring proof

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְאָרֵס הָיוּ בָּהּ מוּמִין אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: that before she was betrothed she had these blemishes,
and his acquisition was a mistaken acquisition.
Before she was betrothed: yes,
from after she was betrothed: no.
phrases.notes: He means proof that the blemishes were there after betrothal, while she was still in her father's house.

phrases.english: But why?
Let us say: they were found here, and they were here!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule of כאן נמצאו וכאן היו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording implies that proof from after betrothal is not enough, but רבא's rule would push such blemishes back to before betrothal.

steps.title: רבא answers: a man checks before he marries
steps.stepSummary: For blemishes from after betrothal, even if we push them back earlier, a man checks a woman before betrothing her. So he must have seen them and accepted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About after she was betrothed, we can say there is a presumption that a person does not drink from a cup unless he checks it first. This man saw the blemishes and was satisfied.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule. He explains why proof from after betrothal does not help the husband, even if we assume the blemishes were there earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing the blemishes back to before betrothal does not win the case for the husband. There is a חזקה that a man checks a woman before betrothing her, like checking a cup before drinking. So if the blemishes were there, he saw them and accepted them, and it is not a mistaken deal.

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם שׁוֹתֶה בְּכוֹס אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בּוֹדְקוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person does not drink from a cup unless he checks it first
He checks it
He saw and was satisfied, he accepted it
Because one can say

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first defense is that a man checks before he betroths, so he saw the blemishes and accepted them. The very next step shows this reason does not hold up by itself, and step 16 replaces it with a two-presumption answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: From after she was betrothed,
it is because one can say:
there is a presumption that a person does not drink from a cup
unless he checks it.
And this one saw and was satisfied.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a separate presumption that blocks the husband's claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Proof from after betrothal should help the husband, since by רבא's rule the blemishes go back to before betrothal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, the husband checked her before betrothing and accepted the blemishes, so there is no mistaken deal.

steps.title: If he checks before betrothal, the 'before betrothal' case should fail too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks step 14. If a man surely checks a woman before betrothal, then even blemishes proven from before אירוסין should count as seen and accepted. Since the משנה does not say that, we must rely on the חזקה that 'a person does not accept blemishes', and that חזקה should apply here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should be true before she was betrothed! So we must be saying there is a חזקה that a person does not accept blemishes. Then here too, say the חזקה that a person does not accept blemishes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 14. The 'he must have checked' logic would also knock out the case the משנה accepts: blemishes from before אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the before-אירוסין case the משנה lets the husband win, even though by step 14's logic he should have seen the blemishes. The only reason he wins is the rule that people do not settle for blemishes. If that rule is strong enough there, it should be strong enough in the after-אירוסין case too, so step 14's answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)
A presumption the law relies on
A person does not agree to accept blemishes
Before she is betrothed

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְאָרֵס נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, before she is betrothed also!
phrases.notes: He means: by your logic, even blemishes from before the betrothal should count as seen and accepted.

phrases.english: Rather, we say:
There is a presumption that a person does not accept blemishes.
Here too,
there should be a presumption that a person does not accept blemishes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְאָרֵס נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14's claim that a man checks a woman before betrothal and so must have accepted her blemishes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That logic would also cancel the before-אירוסין case, which the משנה accepts. So the משנה must rely on 'a person does not accept blemishes', and that חזקה should also help the husband in the after-אירוסין case.

steps.title: After betrothal, two presumptions work against the husband
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: in the after-אירוסין case, two חזקות stand against the husband. העמד הגוף על חזקתו says she was unblemished at betrothal, and 'a person does not drink from a cup without checking it' says he saw her and accepted her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: proof from after she was betrothed does not help him, because there are two presumptions. One: keep the body in its established state. Two: a person does not drink from a cup unless he checks it first. So this man saw her and accepted her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answer and explains the after-אירוסין case a new way. Here there are two presumptions working against the husband, not just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the before-אירוסין case only the 'he checks' presumption works against the husband, so his own presumption (people do not accept blemishes) balances it. After אירוסין, a second presumption is added: we assume her body stayed as it was, so the blemishes came after the betrothal. That gives two presumptions against him.

keyTerms.meaning: From after she was betrothed
Two (here: two presumptions)
Keep the body in its established state

keyTerms.term: אֵין אָדָם שׁוֹתֶה בְּכוֹס אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בּוֹדְקוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person does not drink from a cup without checking it
He saw and was satisfied (accepted it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'he checks' presumption is new here. It was already the reason in step 14. What is new is that it now joins a second presumption, and the two together outweigh the husband's one.

phrases.english: Rather: proof from after she was betrothed does not help,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 13, where the blemishes were proven only from after the betrothal.

phrases.english: because there are two presumptions:
the presumption: keep the body in its established state,
and the presumption: a person does not drink from a cup
unless he checks it first,
phrases.notes: A picture: just as you look at a cup before drinking, a man looks over a woman before marrying her.

phrases.english: and this man saw and was satisfied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15's challenge by giving a new reason for the after-אירוסין case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counting presumptions: two against the husband outweigh his one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's presumption that people do not accept blemishes should help him after אירוסין just as it does before
steps.terutzMaskana: After אירוסין, העמד הגוף על חזקתו joins the 'he checks' presumption, so there are two against him

steps.title: Answering the husband's 'no one accepts blemishes' claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the husband's argument, the חזקה that a person does not accept blemishes, and begins to explain why it cannot win against the two presumptions. The sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do you say, that there is a presumption that a person does not accept blemishes? That is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still finishing its answer from step 16. It brings up the husband's best argument so it can set it aside, and the end of the sentence comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's presumption has not gone away. The גמרא admits it exists and is about to weigh it against the two presumptions from step 16. The full weighing is completed in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: What would you say? (bringing up the other side's argument)
It is / it becomes

steps.whatToRemember: Before אירוסין: one presumption against the husband, balanced by his one, so he can win. After אירוסין: two presumptions against him, so his one presumption is not enough.

that there is a presumption that a person does not accept blemishes
that is...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 16's answer by bringing up the husband's opposing presumption so it can be weighed
